blocks.text: Why requirement gathering is one of the biggest data analyst challenges

The core issue is a disconnect between business needs and data execution. Stakeholders often approach you with a specific output in mind, like a certain chart or a metric. They rarely explain the business problem they are trying to solve. This is a common trap. When you build to a solution rather than a goal, you often miss the mark.

Communication gaps are common. You might have the technical skills to query the database, but you lack the business context. Conversely, stakeholders have the business context but do not understand data constraints. This leads to expectations that do not match reality. You end up delivering a report that technically meets the request but does not answer the business question.
The real cost of poor scoping

Every time you start a task without a clear requirement, you risk rework. This is not just a minor annoyance. It is a major drain on your schedule. You spend hours cleaning data, building models, and formatting dashboards only to hear that it is not what they wanted. This cycle of rework costs 3 to 5 hours per request. It adds up quickly.
How to fix requirement gathering without buying new software

You do not need fancy project management tools to improve your process. Start by implementing a brief or nothing rule. If a stakeholder comes to your desk or sends a slack message, ask them to fill out a simple document. This document should ask for the business problem, the goal, and the expected impact. If they cannot define these, you are not ready to start.

Include the 5 Ws: Who, What, When, Where, Why.
Propose a prototype before building the full solution.
Deliver in iterations to check alignment early.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you manage requirements

Lazur lives in your Mac notch and helps you capture the details during your meetings. When you are in a call, hold the shortcut to ask Lazur to summarize the key points. It can help you draft the initial requirement document based on your notes.
A daily routine for better requirement management
Managing your day is about protecting your time. Use the following routine to keep your focus on high-impact work.

faq.question: Why do stakeholders keep asking for charts instead of insights?
faq.answer: It is often easier for them to visualize a specific output than to articulate a complex business problem. Your job is to gently steer them back to the 'why' by asking what decision they intend to make with the data.

faq.question: Can I use AI to help with requirement gathering?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use tools like Lazur to summarize meeting transcripts or draft documentation. Just ensure you follow your company's data privacy rules regarding sensitive information.

faq.question: What if a stakeholder refuses to write a brief?
faq.answer: Explain the cost of rework. Frame it as a way to ensure they get the right answer faster. Most stakeholders will comply once they realize it saves them time too.

fixes.title: Brief or nothing rule
fixes.text: Require a structured document outlining the business problem before starting any task.

fixes.title: Iterative delivery
fixes.text: Break large projects into small, testable parts to validate assumptions early.

fixes.title: Standardized templates
fixes.text: Use a simple form to collect the 5 Ws for every new data request.
